questions.question: Several services read the setting ChatApp:Model:Deployment from Azure App Configuration. The setting must have one value in the development environment and a different value in production, and the key name must stay the same. What should you use?

options.text: Labels
options.why: Correct. A label lets the same key hold different values, such as dev and prod.

options.text: Snapshots
options.why: A snapshot captures a fixed set of key-values for a release. It does not provide per-environment values for one key.

options.text: Feature flags
options.why: Feature flags turn functionality on or off. They are not used to store per-environment string values.

options.text: Content types
options.why: A content type describes how to interpret a value, not which environment it belongs to.

questions.explanation: Labels differentiate key-values that share a key. Apps select the label for their environment.

questions.question: An application loads its settings from Azure App Configuration. One setting must contain a database password, and the password must remain stored only in Azure Key Vault. What should you add to the App Configuration store?

options.text: A Key Vault reference that contains the URI of the secret
options.why: Correct. A Key Vault reference stores only the secret URI. The app's configuration provider retrieves the value from Key Vault.

options.text: A key-value that contains the password with the content type text/plain
options.why: This stores the password in App Configuration, which violates the requirement.

options.text: A feature flag named password
options.why: Feature flags store on or off state and filters, not secrets.

options.text: A snapshot of the Key Vault secret
options.why: Snapshots capture App Configuration key-values. They cannot capture Key Vault secrets.

questions.explanation: Key Vault references keep secrets in Key Vault while letting the app read all configuration from one source.

questions.scenario: A Python app calls load() from the azure-appconfiguration-provider package with refresh_on=[WatchKey("ChatApp:Sentinel")] and refresh_interval=60. An administrator changes three key-values and then updates ChatApp:Sentinel. The app never shows the new values.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The app does not call the refresh() method on the configuration object
options.why: Correct. refresh_on and refresh_interval define what to watch and how often. The app must call refresh() for a reload to occur.

options.text: The sentinel key must be a feature flag
options.why: A sentinel key is a regular key-value. It does not need to be a feature flag.

options.text: The refresh_interval value must be lower than 30 seconds
options.why: A 60-second interval is valid. It only delays the check.

options.text: The three changed key-values must also be listed in refresh_on
options.why: When the sentinel changes, the provider reloads all selected key-values, so they do not need to be watched individually.

questions.explanation: Dynamic refresh in the Python provider happens when the app calls refresh() and the refresh interval has elapsed.

questions.question: An app uses its managed identity to load settings from Azure App Configuration. Some settings are Key Vault references. Which TWO role assignments does the managed identity require? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: App Configuration Data Reader on the App Configuration store
options.why: Correct. This role allows the app to read key-values from the store.

options.text: Key Vault Secrets User on the key vault
options.why: Correct. The configuration provider in the app retrieves the secret, so the app's identity needs read access to secret values.

options.text: App Configuration Data Owner on the App Configuration store
options.why: This role also allows writes, which exceeds what a reading app needs.

options.text: Key Vault Contributor on the key vault
options.why: Key Vault Contributor manages the vault resource and does not grant access to secret values.

questions.explanation: Reading configuration needs App Configuration Data Reader. Resolving Key Vault references needs Key Vault Secrets User because the app, not App Configuration, reads the secret.

questions.question: You plan to release a new version of an AI service. Production must load exactly the set of key-values that was tested, and the set must not change after the release, even if someone edits the store. What should you use?

options.text: An App Configuration snapshot
options.why: Correct. A snapshot is an immutable, named set of key-values that an app can load by name.

options.text: A sentinel key
options.why: A sentinel key triggers a reload of current values. It does not freeze them.

options.text: A label named release
options.why: Key-values with a label can still be edited, so the set could change.

options.text: A feature flag with a targeting filter
options.why: Targeting controls which users see a feature. It does not freeze configuration values.

questions.explanation: Snapshots are read-only after creation, which makes releases repeatable and rollbacks simple.
